title: Apply crop protection and animal health products effectively and responsibly

lessons.title: Planning and mixing at the correct dose
lessons.html:
The pre-application plan

Before any spraying or dipping, your supervisor makes a plan. You must understand it and check it with them. The plan says:

  • which product to use and why (the pest, disease, weed or parasite),
  • which field, block or group of animals,
  • the dose rate and the amount of water,
  • which equipment to use,
  • the PPE needed,
  • the re-entry and withholding periods on the label.

Only use products registered under Act 36 of 1947 for that crop or animal. The label is the law: it tells you how to use the product.

Check the weather and the area

  • Do not spray in strong wind. Spray drift can harm people, animals, bees, water and the neighbour's crops.
  • Do not spray if rain is coming soon, unless the label allows it.
  • Keep away from dams, rivers and boreholes.
  • Warn other workers and put up warning signs.

Check the equipment

Check the sprayer, hoses, nozzles and dip tank for leaks and blockages. A calibrated sprayer gives the right amount. Your supervisor will show you how to check the output.

Mixing

  1. Put on full PPE before opening the container.
  2. Mix in a safe place, away from water sources, on a surface where spills can be cleaned up.
  3. Half-fill the tank with clean water.
  4. Measure the product exactly with a measuring jug or scale kept only for chemicals. Never guess.
  5. Add the product, then fill up with water while the agitator runs.
  6. Triple-rinse empty containers and pour the rinse water into the tank.

Too little product will not work, and pests can become resistant. Too much wastes money, harms the crop or animal, and leaves residues on food.

lessons.title: Applying safely
lessons.html:
Applying to crops

  • Walk or drive at the steady speed you used for calibration.
  • Keep the boom or nozzle at the right height so the spray covers the plants evenly.
  • Spray with the wind behind you or from the side, so the spray moves away from you.
  • Do not spray over people, animals, water or houses.
  • Stop if the wind picks up.

Applying to animals

Animal health products include dips, pour-ons, sprays and drenches against ticks, lice, flies and worms.

  • Weigh or estimate the animals' mass if the dose depends on mass.
  • Keep the dip tank at the right strength, as the label and your supervisor say.
  • Do not dip animals that are hot, tired, thirsty or very young unless the label says it is safe.
  • Handle animals calmly in the crush or race.

Protecting yourself

PPEWhy
Chemical-resistant glovesMost poisoning happens through the skin
Overall or apronProtects body and clothes
Rubber boots, trousers over the bootsStops spray running into boots
Goggles or face shieldProtects the eyes
Respirator, if the label saysStops you breathing in fumes or dust

Never

  • Never eat, drink or smoke while working with chemicals.
  • Never blow out a blocked nozzle with your mouth. Use a soft brush or water.
  • Never put chemicals in food or drink bottles.
  • Never work alone with highly toxic products.
  • Never let children or untrained people near the mixing site.

Working with others

Agree on hand signals with the tractor driver or team leader before spraying starts, so that you can stop the work quickly if there is a problem. Keep bystanders, children and animals out of the area being treated until the re-entry time on the label has passed.

lessons.title: After application, reporting and emergencies
lessons.html:
Post-application procedures

  1. Clean the sprayer: rinse the tank, hoses and nozzles, and spray the rinse water onto the treated area, as the label allows.
  2. Triple-rinse empty containers, puncture them so they cannot be reused, and take them to the place your farm uses for chemical waste.
  3. Store unused product in the locked chemical store, in its original container.
  4. Wash your PPE, then wash yourself with soap and water. Wash work clothes separately from family clothes.
  5. Put up or leave up the warning signs until the re-entry period is over.
  6. Fill in the spray or treatment record: date, product, dose, area or animals treated, operator and weather.

Monitor and report

Tell your supervisor about anything unusual: a blocked nozzle, a leak, drift, burnt leaves, sick animals, pests still present, or a product that looked different. Report what you saw, where and when.

Emergencies

Signs of poisoning can include headache, dizziness, sweating, nausea, vomiting, blurred vision, tight chest and twitching. If you or a colleague show these signs:

  1. Stop work and move the person away from the chemical into fresh air.
  2. Remove contaminated clothing.
  3. Wash skin with lots of clean water and soap. For eyes, rinse with clean running water for at least 15 minutes.
  4. Do not make the person vomit unless the label or a doctor says so.
  5. Get medical help at once and take the product label with you.

A national poison information helpline can give advice; your farm should display the number at the chemical store.

Spills

Keep people and animals away. Wear PPE. Stop the spill and cover it with sand or soil, then scoop it into a container for safe disposal. Never wash a spill into a drain or river. Report every spill.

Key points

  • Follow the pre-application plan and the label: the label is the law.
  • Measure the product exactly and check the weather before spraying.
  • Wear full PPE and never eat, drink or smoke with chemicals.
  • Clean equipment, dispose of containers safely and keep records.
  • In poisoning, remove the person from the chemical, wash and get medical help with the label.
